title: Console GTM readiness: dashboards, rollout controls, and cost breakdown — training & release notes coordination
creator: Anika Rao
description: Coordinate cross-functional readiness for the upcoming Console UX features: per-route dashboards (latency/cost), rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallbacks), and token-level cost breakdowns. Deliverables: final release notes, internal training, partner-facing one-pager, support-runbook, and synchronized go/no-go checklist with Eng, Design, Support, Sales Engineering, and Docs.
acceptance_criteria: Release notes drafted, reviewed by Eng/Design/Legal, and published to docs.redwood.ai/release-notes before GA
Two internal training sessions scheduled and recorded; slides + quick reference checklist available
Support runbook in Confluence with troubleshooting steps and escalation path
Marketing comms approved and scheduled; partner one-pager uploaded to Drive
Go/No-Go matrix completed with SLO, regression, and infra capacity checks passed
checklist: Eng review of cost breakdown language — requested change 2026-03-04
Design signoff on dashboard screenshots and copy — complete
Create training deck & quickstart scripts — assigned to Liam
Support runbook draft — assigned to Priya (Support)
Publish release notes and docs page
Post-launch monitoring plan & dashboard — ENG to provide link
stakeholders: Engineering: Mateo Ruiz (Lead) - infra & API compatibility
Design: Mei Chen - screenshots & UX copy
Docs: Sofia Hall - release notes & how-to
Sales Eng: Robert Kim - partner play
training_plan: Two 45-minute sessions: internal product walkthrough + Q&A (2026-03-17), partner-focused hands-on lab (2026-03-19). Deliverables: deck, 10-min recorded demo, 3-slide quickstart, FAQ. Trainer: Liam O'Connell. Recordings to be uploaded to internal learning site.
comms_plan: Internal: All-engineering + Support announcement email (2026-03-20), dedicated Slack channel #console-launch-2026
External: Blog post + product update email targeted to active customers (coord with Marketing), partner one-pager for SEs
Release notes: Short summary + migration notes for customers using dedicated/private deployments
Social: Product highlight thread for developer community; coordinate with OSS/community team
launch_plan: Pre-launch week: run canary on 10% traffic using rollout control; monitor latency, error rate, and token-cost regressions
Go/No-Go: final readiness review 2026-03-20 with PM/Eng/Support/Legal
GA: release window 2026-03-21 09:00 UTC; publish release notes and blog post after GA confirmation
Post-launch (48-72h): elevated support rotations + daily regression checks
risks: Cost breakdown language could be misinterpreted by customers leading to support volume spike
Rollout control bug could cause inconsistent behavior across regions — mitigation: canary + automatic rollback policy
Docs/Release notes not clear on Dedicated/Private upgrade path — mitigation: include explicit migration steps and contact points
Training attendance low for SEs leading to gaps in partner messaging — mitigation: record sessions and require on-demand module completion
decisions: Use canary rollout at 10% for first 48 hours; auto-fallback to previous model if token-cost > 1.2x baseline
Cost breakdown UI will show estimated token cost per call and a link to billing docs (deferred deeper cost analytics to Optimize 2.0)
No special security review required for UI changes; any backend telemetry that contains PII must be gated (Eng to follow up)

2026-03-10 - Training slides v0.9 uploaded; requested additions: a troubleshooting FAQ and a 'what to promise' quickline for SEs
notes: Keep messaging precise on cost estimates (range + assumptions). Coordinate timing with any infra maintenance windows. Track post-launch metrics: support ticket volume by topic, regression rate on latency and 95th pct, and adoption of rollout controls by org.
